title: Grateful Dead Live at Wembley Empire Pool on 1972-04-07
lineage: 2 AUD sources: MR> C> CDR + M?> low-gen reel> CDR (see info file)

ai_review.summary: A legendary Europe ’72 performance shines through, but the audience‑only tapes are virtually unlistenable.
ai_review.review: The show captured on gd72-04-07.aud.hanno.6161.sbeok.shnf is one of the standout early‑1972 concerts – the first set rolls with relentless energy and the second set delivers a monster The Other One/Truckin'/Wharf Rat sequence, superb Jerry solos, Phil’s bass fireworks and Bill’s other‑worldly drumming.  Unfortunately both audience (AUD) sources are described as horrendous – muffled, crackling and at times sounding like it was recorded from the bottom of a pool – making the recording essentially for completists only.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (average show rating ≈4.0) while nearly all condemn the audio quality (average recording rating ≈1.5). Weighted 70 % show + 30 % recording gives a combined score around 3.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Both AUD sources are described as horrendous, muffled, crackly and inconsistent – likened to being recorded from the bottom of a pool or with a mic stuck in a vent.  The first AUD track is marginally listenable; the second is “stunningly awful”.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is high‑octane and fast, second set builds into an epic Meat sequence (Truckin' → Drums → The Other One → El Paso → Wharf Rat) that many fans cite as a tour highlight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for blistering tone, soaring solos (especially on Truckin') and overall fiery playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “bombs” on bass, a caution‑tease near the end of The Other One, and generally strong low‑end work.
band_member_comments.Bob: Described as “on fire”, delivering powerful vocals; his organ work receives mixed comments (some dislike Pigpen’s organ, others enjoy it).
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s interplay with Jerry on Wharf Rat is highlighted positively; overall keyboard presence is less discussed but not criticized.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming in the Meat sequence is called “other‑worldly” and a major factor in the show’s intensity.
